newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish mixed after rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish mixed after rally.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly mixed after setting highs in the morning, selling off on technicals at midday and staging a brief, late rally.
One trader said the late rally in December S&P 500 index futures "killed the bears," but buying power ebbed near the close of pit trading.
Some volatility was seen linked to expiration of November Standard & Poor's 100 index options and individual equity options, which traders said had a slight negative net impact.
December Standard & Poor's 500 index futures set a contract high at 745.50 in the morning, then dipped at midday.
Traders said momentum in S&P 500s carried over from Thursday's rally and on huge buyside New York Stock Exchange pre-opening order imbalances.
Selling at midday followed U.S. Treasury bond futures down on profit-taking based on a perception that an earlier T-bond rally was overdone, traders said.
S&P 500s held above support at 736.20, then rose on short covering and as T-bond futures cut losses into their close, one trader said.
Preclosing NYSE order imbalances tilted to the buy side, further fueling the late rally, traders said.
Fair value on Friday was about 2.10 points over cash. Some traders expected arbitrage buy programs near 2.90 premium.

Arb sell programs needed a premium over cash of roughly 1.30 points or less. Brokers saw occasional buy programs during the morning and sell programs during the afternoon when the NYSE's curb on index arbitrage programs was not in effect.

Dec S&P 500s rose 1.60 points to close at 740.85, Midcap 400s fell 0.45 to 253.70, Value Lines fell 1.20 to 669.60, NYSE Composites rose 0.90 to 391.60, NASDAQ 100 futures fell 9.45 to 805.75, and the Nikkei 225 fell 85.0 to 21,020.0.
